final_candidates.decision_summary: Analog of spike N501Y, a documented affinity-enhancing substitution at the RBD-ACE2 interface that forms pi contacts with Y41 of ACE2. WT residue verified as N at position 171.
Analog of spike S477N, observed in lineages with improved ACE2 binding via added hydrogen bonding. WT residue verified as S at position 147.
Analog of spike Q493R, a core RBM interface residue whose basic side chain can strengthen electrostatic contacts with ACE2. WT residue verified as Q at position 163.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are well-motivated interface mutations with residue identities verified; further rounds without external evidence would not change the ranking.

history.rationale: N501Y (local 171) is the best-characterized RBD mutation that strengthens ACE2 binding via new tyrosine–Y41/ACE2 contacts, and is compatible with folded RBD as seen in Alpha/Beta variants.
Equivalent to spike N501Y, a well-documented ACE2-binding-enhancing substitution at the RBD-ACE2 interface; residue verified as N at position 171.
S477N (local 147) arose repeatedly and enhances ACE2 affinity by adding a contact with ACE2 S19 region while maintaining structure.
Equivalent to spike S477N, observed in variants with improved ACE2 affinity; WT residue verified as S at 147.
N439K (local 109) mildly increases ACE2 binding and was widely circulating, indicating good tolerability and slight affinity gain.
This position is not a known affinity hotspot and a glycosylation-site change could destabilize folding; downgrading in favor of better-supported interface mutations.
Y453F (local 123) is reported to increase human ACE2 binding; conservative aromatic substitution likely preserves RBD core packing.
Conservative aromatic substitution near interface Y453 (spike numbering) region; plausible but unverified benefit.
Q498Y (local 168) is predicted/biochemically reported to strengthen the RBD–ACE2 interface (used in design with N501Y), though alone its effect is less certain.
Q498Y analog can add hydrophobic/aromatic contact at the ACE2 interface; moderate confidence.
T478K (local 148) from Delta improves ACE2 affinity and is structurally tolerated at the receptor-binding ridge.
Surface charge change with uncertain directional effect on binding; kept as lower-priority option.
L452R (local 122) modestly increases ACE2 binding and is compatible with stability, though it is partly selected for immune escape.
Hydrophobic-to-charged substitution in the RBM core is more likely to disrupt local structure than improve binding.

rejection.reason: Hydrophobic-to-charged substitution in the RBM core is more likely to disrupt local structure than improve binding.

history.rationale: E484K (local 154) is viable and reduces antibody binding; any direct ACE2 benefit is small, so ranked lower for the affinity objective.
E484K analog is more associated with antibody escape than affinity gain; retaining but lowering priority.
Q493R (local 163) from Beta alters a salt bridge with ACE2 K31/E35 and may compensate for K417N loss, but alone affinity gain is uncertain.
Equivalent to spike Q493R, a core RBM interface residue that can strengthen ACE2 contact; raising confidence above less-supported candidates.
K417N (local 87) is well tolerated but generally decreases ACE2 affinity; retained only for reconsideration as a compensatory pairing.
Position is outside the receptor-binding motif and unlikely to affect ACE2 binding; removes an active-pool slot.

rejection.reason: Position is outside the receptor-binding motif and unlikely to affect ACE2 binding; removes an active-pool slot.
